prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats’ 2024 manifesto promises a “Fair Deal” built on five themes: a stronger, greener economy; high-quality public services; protection of nature and climate; an outward-looking UK with a fair international order; and a revitalised democracy.

- Economy and business: Drive growth via renewables, home insulation and an industrial strategy focused on future skills and technologies; Lifelong Skills Grants and more apprenticeships; overhaul parental leave; back small firms and replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; fix UK–EU trade; manage public finances responsibly; reverse Conservatives’ bank tax cuts; impose a proper windfall tax on oil and gas; raise personal allowance when affordable; increase Digital Services Tax; fair CGT reform; 4% tax on FTSE buybacks; expand the British Business Bank; clear AI rules; invest 3–3.5% of GDP in R&D; nationwide gigabit broadband.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; 10‑year home upgrade programme (free for low‑income households), zero‑carbon new homes; social energy tariff, decouple electricity from gas; ban fracking and new coal; expand storage, interconnectors and community energy; Net Zero Delivery Authority and citizens’ assemblies; restore aid to 0.7% with climate focus.

- Health and care: Right to see a GP in 7 days/24 hours urgent, with 8,000 more GPs; restore NHS dentistry access; mental health hubs in every community and a professional in every school; cancer treatment within 62 days; boost public health; workforce retention and independent pay review; Patients’ Charter and better NHS tech; shift drugs policy to health, with a regulated cannabis market; free personal care; Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour) and Royal College; paid carers’ leave and respite; cross‑party social care funding deal.

- Education and families: Per‑pupil funding rising above inflation; fix crumbling buildings; Tutoring Guarantee; early‑years boost and tripled EYPP; reinstate maintenance grants; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants; teacher recruitment and CPD strategy; SEND overhaul; free school meals for all children in poverty; parental leave/pay reforms (double statutory pay, more for fathers/partners, day‑one rights incl. self‑employed); childcare funding reform; return to Erasmus+.

- Welfare and pensions: Scrap the two‑child limit and benefit cap; target ending deep poverty; UC first payment in 5 days; scrap bedroom tax; protect the triple lock; fair redress for 1950s women; raise and widen Carer’s Allowance; fix Statutory Sick Pay.

- Housing and communities: Build 380,000 homes a year (150,000 social); ban no‑fault evictions; default three‑year tenancies and landlord register; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; end rough sleeping; rent‑to‑own for social housing; empower councils on Right to Buy and second homes; plan-led, zero‑carbon development.

- Environment and farming: End the sewage scandal (new regulator, bonus bans, sewage tax, real‑time data); “double nature” by 2050; Clean Air Act; 60m trees/year; deposit return scheme and rapid cut in single‑use plastics; add £1bn/year to Environmental Land Management; uphold food, welfare and environmental standards; EU veterinary/plant health deals.

- Transport: Accelerate EV switch (charging rollout, plug‑in grant, 2030 ZEV mandate); freeze/simplify rail fares; major electrification and Northern Powerhouse Rail; empower bus franchising and keep £2 cap while reviewed; national active travel plan; more road maintenance; fairer aviation taxes and curb short flights with viable rail.

- Immigration, rights and democracy: End the Hostile Environment; scrap the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; process asylum claims within 3 months and allow work after 3; expand safe/legal routes; flexible, sector‑led work visas; protect EU citizens; champion the Human Rights Act; ban conversion therapy; proportional representation (STV), Lords reform, cap donations, votes at 16, written federal constitution.

- Defence and international: Reverse Army cuts and raise defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; retain the nuclear deterrent; procurement reform and better support for personnel; rebuild ties with Europe via a four‑stage roadmap toward the Single Market and long‑term EU membership; stand with Ukraine (including seizing Russian assets); press for an Israel–Gaza ceasefire and a two‑state solution; restore 0.7% aid and an independent development department; fund the BBC World Service.
